chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Abdullah ibn al-Mughira, from Abdullah ibn Sinan, who said:

I asked him (peace be upon him) about an old man who was weakened from fasting the month of Ramadan. He (peace be upon him) said: 'He should give in charity every day with what suffices as a meal of a poor one'.
ai.seo_question: What is the ruling for an old person who cannot fast due to weakness?
ai.summary: This narration from al-Kafi clarifies the specific mechanism of fidyah for the elderly, emphasizing daily sustenance for a poor person rather than a lump-sum payment, a view supported by many Shia jurists. It highlights the practical application of the principle of ease (taysir) in Islamic law, ensuring that those permanently unable to fast are not burdened beyond their capacity while maintaining their spiritual obligation through charity.
